title: Cost-based variable selection via harm-adjusted net benefit
setting: Synthetic logistic-outcome data (1000 train, 4000 held-out rows) with 6 predictors: 3 cheap informative, 1 expensive informative (weak or strong), and 2 noise. Three selectors choose a subset: exhaustive search on CV net benefit minus measurement harm, backward elimination on CV log-loss, or CV-tuned L1 logistic regression. The chosen model is refit, and the metric is held-out net benefit at threshold pt minus the summed harm of the selected variables.

paper.title: Cost-based variable selection for prediction models
paper.claim: Selecting variables by cross-validated net benefit minus measurement harm yields higher harm-adjusted clinical utility and fewer costly predictors than cost-blind backward elimination or LASSO.

metric.name: adj_net_benefit
metric.description: Held-out net benefit TP/n - FP/n*pt/(1-pt) of the refit model on the selected variables, minus the summed measurement harm of those variables. Diagnostics: raw_net_benefit, n_selected, expensive_selected, auc.

factors.name: method
factors.description: Variable selection: backward elimination on CV log-loss (cost-blind), exhaustive cost-based net-benefit search (paper), or L1 logistic regression with CV penalty (cost-blind).

factors.name: expensive_harm
factors.description: Net-benefit harm of measuring the expensive predictor (cheap predictors cost 0.001 each).

factors.name: expensive_coef
factors.description: True logistic coefficient of the expensive predictor (weak vs strong signal).

factors.name: pt
factors.description: Decision threshold probability used for net benefit; sets the weight of false positives.
